The degree of the court whose judgment starts this period. Empty: any.
The courts whose judgments start this period. Leave empty for any court.
Civil Procedure Law 83 of 1969, Art. 25(2): a period that ends on an official holiday ends on the next working day.
Recording a judgment of this law and court degree creates this deadline by itself. Other periods are added by hand, by a session outcome or by the period before them.
An absolute cap counted from the decision, e.g. correction of a cassation decision.
The period that starts when this one ends without an answer (silence counts as rejection).
Missing the period forfeits the right, and the court rejects a late challenge on its own motion (Civil Procedure Law 83 of 1969, Art. 171).

A period counts from the day after this event (Civil Procedure Law Art. 25(1)). End of the previous period: it starts when the period before it ends without an answer, since silence counts as a rejection.
For periods that a session outcome starts, e.g. a case left for review.
Verified: read in the law's own text. Secondary: taken from commentary or a practice guide. Unverified: check it before relying on it at a court.
Type of the exception activity on record.
Icon to indicate an exception activity.

Status based on activities
Overdue: Due date is already passed
Today: Activity date is today
Planned: Future activities.
What the client still owes on posted invoices, in the company's currency.
The contact used for letters, invoices and portal access.
Due instalments, approved time and recharged expenses not yet invoiced, in the company's currency.
How long a copy of this document can be relied on.
Earlier appearances that are not a conflict, such as the same opponent in another of our matters.
Waiting: for documents, for the body's answer, or for confirmation that a document is genuine.
The person who must act on the letter.
The correspondence register is switched on: letters get numbers.
Working days from the date the letter was received (incoming) or sent (outgoing) to the date an answer is due.
Set when a reply to this letter is registered, or by hand when it was answered some other way.
The number stays in the book, struck through, with this reason next to it.
The last day after moving off a holiday where the law allows it.
The last day of the period counted in calendar days. Act by this date.
Off for a period that runs for the other side (a judgment in our favour) or for an authority (the time it has to answer a grievance). Such a period ends unused, not missed.
The period ends on a weekend or holiday, so the law gives until the next working day.
Ended unused: a period that belonged to the other side or to an authority ended without anyone acting on it. Nothing was missed on our side.
Title used at the head of official letters, e.g. the director general.
The court that hears appeals or cassation from this court.
Iraqi Bar administrative order 3021 of 2021 on company legal-adviser retainers.
Can be combined with any arrangement, e.g. a lump sum plus a success fee.
Used for expenses whose category has no account of its own.
Matters whose target date or next date falls in the period.
Leave empty to hand the work over for good. With a date the colleague covers until then: they join the teams and take the work dated up to that day.
Written once into the history of every matter that changes hands.
The case number at the current court stage. Earlier numbers stay on the court stages.
What must be ready for the next session. It becomes a to-do for the responsible lawyer a few working days before the session.
Courts usually keep the session's time; change it if the court set another.
For a suspension: the day the agreed suspension ends. The case must be resumed within the period after it.
The date is an estimate until the endowment offices announce it.
Leave empty for a holiday in all of Iraq.
The number the court gives the challenge, if known.
Plain text with placeholders in braces, for example {matter_number}, {client}, {body}, {today}, {responsible}. Nothing else is evaluated.
Which step offers this message to a client.
Used for deadlines at this authority's departments that have no calendar of their own.
The due date of the last period for which a matter was opened.
Who the matters are opened for. Empty: the client's responsible.
The day the matter for the next due date is opened.
For example: the client ended the mandate by notarial notice number and date.
A matter type whose documents to collect make up the pack, e.g. a tender file.
For a lawsuit, the date of the first session; otherwise the date the work is due.
Only the responsible, the team and legal managers can see a confidential matter.
When the matter was last sent for approval.
The date the body should have answered, counted in working days on its calendar from the day the file was submitted.
A planned court session whose day has come and whose outcome is not recorded yet.
Working days the body usually takes: from the matter type, else from the body.
The number the government body gave the file, or the client's own reference.
Date of the next planned court session or counter visit.

The client's records hold a copy of this document that is valid today.
The client's original is in our custody and must be returned (Advocacy Law Art. 53).
Number of the body's confirmation letter, or the QR reference of a notary document.
Recharged to the client on the next invoice (Advocacy Law Art. 55).

Decides which appeal periods apply and whether the fee cap applies.

Working days after the reference date at which the step is due.
What must be brought or answered before the body continues, e.g. the tax clearance letter.
Who has to act next. While the body has the file, the days at the body are counted.
The person who sent a matter for approval cannot approve it themselves.
Working days and public holidays used to count legal deadlines and step offsets. When empty, the company's own working calendar is used.
Law office: a matter that starts work without a signed fee agreement is flagged. Advocacy Law Art. 65: fee claims without a written agreement lapse after 3 years.
Advocacy Law 173 of 1965, Art. 56: fees may not exceed 20% of the matter's value, except in criminal matters.

Registration numbers, a document vault with expiry dates, letters of guarantee and recurring obligations for each company.
Transactions at ministries and departments: services, counter visits, the documents to carry.
